settledUnits.title: Settled units
settledUnits.content:
Settled units is the number of residential lots/homes that legally transferred to buyers (and were recognised as revenue) in the period -- the single volume driver behind the whole income statement for a land developer.

For Winton Land Limited: settlements collapsed from 565 (FY2023) to just 266 (FY2025) and a near-halt of 14 units in H1 FY2026, then rebounded to 430 for the full FY2026 year as deferred H1 settlements pushed into H2 -- read the FY total, not the H1 print, as the cycle signal.

What to watch:

  • H1 vs H2 skew (settlement timing, not underlying demand, can swing a half)
  • Units settled against the pre-sale book -- a shrinking book with rising settlements means the pipeline is being drawn down, not replenished
  • Consent/construction delays that push settlements between fiscal years

avgRevenuePerUnit.title: Average revenue per settled unit
avgRevenuePerUnit.content:
Average revenue per unit is reported segment revenue divided by units settled in the period (NZ$ thousands) -- it separates price/mix from volume in the revenue line.

For Winton Land Limited: per-unit revenue has drifted up (from ~$346k-355k in FY2022 to $439k in FY2026) as the mix shifted toward higher-value South Island (Queenstown-Lakes) product and commercial/hospitality contribution, which partly offsets the fall in unit volume.

What to watch:

  • Whether rising per-unit revenue is mix (more premium lots) or genuine price growth
  • Discounting to move stock in a soft market would show up here before it shows up in the margin lines

preSaleBook.title: Contracted pre-sale book
preSaleBook.content:
Pre-sale book is the value of contracted sales (deposits taken, unconditional or near-unconditional) not yet settled -- the closest thing a land developer has to a revenue backlog, disclosed at each result date rather than derived from the accounts.

For Winton Land Limited: the book fell from $239.8m at Dec-25 (H1 FY2026) to $27.4m at Jun-26 (FY2026) as the backlog converted into FY2026's settlement rebound without being refilled -- this is the single clearest forward-looking warning sign in the business, pointing to another thin settlement period ahead unless new pre-sales are written.

What to watch:

  • Book size relative to one year's typical settlement revenue (a $27m book funds only a fraction of a normal year)
  • New pre-sales written each half versus the prior book, not just the closing balance
  • Concentration in a single project (e.g. Sunfield, still subject to the Auckland Council High Court challenge) that could delay conversion

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Winton Land Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Winton Land Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Winton Land Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Winton Land Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Winton Land Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Winton Land Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Winton Land Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Winton Land Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is mostly land/housing settlement revenue recognised when title transfers, plus a growing slice of recurring commercial and hospitality income (Cracker Bay, Ayrburn, Northbrook Wānaka).

For Winton Land Limited: this is a lumpy, settlement-driven line, not a smooth subscription-style series -- see the Settled Units and Pre-sale Book charts above for the volume and forward-visibility story behind the swings (e.g. H1 FY2026's 60% YoY revenue collapse on just 14 units settled, versus FY2026's full-year 21.5% rebound).

What to watch:

  • Units settled and pre-sale book, not the revenue print in isolation
  • H1 vs H2 skew from settlement timing
  • Growing share from recurring commercial/hospitality assets versus one-off land sales

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Winton Land Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
